items.title: Syncing two desktop clients
items.text:
Use this procedure to check changes traveling through altero between two real Zotero Desktop installations. It is useful for reporting a platform or deployment that the automated tests do not cover.

Use disposable data and separate profiles. Preserve a failed run for diagnosis before starting again. For automated checks, see Desktop compatibility checks.

items.title: Test setup
items.text:
Use:

  • a dedicated altero instance;
  • one test account;
  • two separate Zotero profiles/data directories; and
  • the same API and streaming endpoints in both profiles.

The two clients should represent two installations of the same account, not two unrelated personal libraries.

For a test on Windows or macOS, use two computers or create test profiles using Zotero's profile instructions. Before linking either profile, verify that its data directory is empty and different from your everyday library and the other test profile. Check the directory in Settings → Advanced → Files and Folders. You can run the two profiles one at a time; simultaneous instances also require separate profile and data directories.

items.title: Configure both clients
items.text:
Each Zotero profile needs:

extensions.zotero.api.url = http://localhost:8000/
extensions.zotero.streaming.url = ws://localhost:8000/stream

Restart Zotero and link the same altero account in both profiles.

For a remote server, replace localhost:8000 with the server's public address and use https:// and wss:// together. Set attachment syncing to Zotero and file downloads to at sync time on both clients, so this test exercises altero's file store.

For the complete linking flow, see Connecting a Zotero client.

items.title: Before testing
items.text:
Check that each profile has its own empty data directory and that both use the same altero account. Do not use your everyday Zotero library. Set both API and streaming URLs; the API setting alone does not redirect streaming.

Wait until both clients finish syncing before comparing them. An unresolved sync error or queued change means the test has not settled.

items.title: Suggested test sequence
items.text:
Start with a small library and exercise operations that require both directions of sync.

  1. Create several item types on client A and sync.
  2. Confirm they appear on client B.
  3. Add collections, tags, notes and attachments on B and sync back to A.
  4. Edit the same item on both clients while one is offline, then reconnect it.
  5. Move items between collections.
  6. Trash and restore items.
  7. Delete an object and confirm the other client learns the deletion.
  8. Change an attachment and verify the file reaches the other client.
  9. Exercise a group library if the test instance has one.
  10. Repeat a sync with no changes and confirm the library does not advance unnecessarily.

The important result is convergence: after all syncs finish, both clients and the server agree on the library state.

items.title: Compare the libraries
items.text:
The repository includes a comparison tool for two local Zotero data directories against the server:

uv run python tools/compare_libraries.py --key <api-key> \
  A=~/zotero-test/A/data \
  B=~/zotero-test/B/data

Use it after the clients report that synchronization is complete.

A passing test should not require manual database repair, object-version changes or a reset of either client.

items.title: Testing group libraries
items.text:
One account on both clients is still useful for group-library sync because it tests two installations of the same member.

Use additional accounts only when you are specifically testing group membership, permissions, ownership or per-member restrictions.

items.title: Record enough information to reproduce failures
items.text:
When a run fails, record:

  • Zotero version;
  • operating system;
  • altero revision/version;
  • SQLite or PostgreSQL;
  • deployment method;
  • the exact operation being synced;
  • which client made each change;
  • the error shown by Zotero; and
  • server logs that do not contain private library data or API keys.

items.title: When the run is complete
items.text:
Keep failed state until you have a reproduction or report. After a successful run, the disposable instance and profiles can be removed.

A clean two-client run is stronger evidence than replaying captured HTTP traffic because it exercises the real client's local synchronization state in both directions.

The automated acceptance runner creates disposable profiles and checks disjoint offline edits, file bytes, trash/restore, child deletion and schema serialization using the real sync engine. Keep this manual procedure for same-field conflict dialogs and group-removal prompts on other platforms too; the automated runner already drives those dialogs on Linux.

items.title: Windows and macOS reports
items.text:
Windows and macOS have not completed the project's automated desktop acceptance suite. A community basic-sync report does not cover the checks below. A manual run records evidence for its checked operations; it does not certify the full automated matrix.

Use the setup and sequence above, then record pass, fail or not run for each case. Sync both clients until idle after each change, and check the browser library as a third view of the server's metadata.

Check Operation and expected result Linking and restart Link each fresh profile, restart it, and sync again without another approval or error. Metadata both ways Create a book with a creator, Unicode title and tag on A. On B, change its title and add a child note. All three views agree. Collection graph Create nested collections, file the book, then move a collection on B. The hierarchy and memberships agree. Disjoint offline edits Disable automatic sync on both. Change the title on A and the date on B; sync A, B, A. Both changes survive. Conflict dialog With automatic sync off, change the same title differently on both. Sync A, then B, choose a side in the dialog, then sync A. Repeat choosing the other side. All views agree with each choice. Trash and deletion Trash the book, restore it, then trash and permanently delete it. Sync between steps. Both clients and the browser show each transition and remove its children at deletion. Stored files Attach a small PDF and a file with a Unicode filename on A. On B, open the downloaded files and compare their actual bytes with the originals. Repeat from B to A. File replacement Change a stored file on B, sync B then A, and verify A's bytes. Restart both clients and verify the files still open. Browser edits Edit a field and child note and upload a file through the browser. Both clients receive the edits and matching file bytes. Live updates Re-enable automatic sync and restart both. Leave B idle; change and sync A. B receives the change without pressing Sync. Record separately if only manual sync works. Groups If available, repeat metadata and file checks in a group. With a second, read-only member, confirm reading works and editing is unavailable. Otherwise mark this not run. Settled sync Sync both twice without further edits. No recurring error, conflict or repeated upload appears.

Report results in issue #49, including successful runs. Copy this outline and fill in every row above:

Date:
Client A: OS version / architecture / exact Zotero version:
Client B: OS version / architecture / exact Zotero version:
altero version or commit:
Database: SQLite / PostgreSQL version:
Deployment: Docker / Podman / source; reverse proxy and TLS setup:
Test profiles with separate, empty data directories: yes / no
Results: check name — pass / fail / not run; observations
Failure: steps, expected result, actual result, and exact error
Recovery required: none / describe

Record the first failing step before trying recovery. Keep the disposable state for a reproduction. Share only logs and screenshots you have checked for API keys, session tokens, authorization headers, passwords and private library data.

items.title: The web interface
items.text:
Open /app/ on your altero server to work with your library in a browser. You can create and edit references, write notes, manage files and collections, and share work. Changes synchronize with Zotero Desktop.

Signing into the browser does not sign Zotero Desktop in. Connect the desktop application using its own setup guide.

items.title: Choose a task
items.text:
Task Guide Sign in, change settings or manage credentials Accounts and personal settings Search, edit, organize or merge references Browsing and organizing a library Publish work or share a collection Publishing and sharing Move a library, make a backup or export references Moving, importing and exporting data Join or manage a group Groups, invitations and activity Manage the server and its accounts Administration

Registration may be closed. Ask the administrator for an account or use a group invitation. If your organization requires institutional sign-in, use the provider button on the sign-in page.

items.title: Installing it as an app
items.text:
You can give altero its own app window:

  • iPhone or iPad: open it in Safari, then choose Share → Add to Home Screen. This has not been verified on a real device.
  • Android, Chrome or Edge: choose Install in the browser menu or address bar.

The app needs a network connection to show your library. It does not keep an offline library. When an interface update is available, choose Reload to load it.

items.title: When to use Zotero Desktop
items.text: Use Zotero Desktop for offline library access, PDF annotation and other reader workflows. The browser note editor preserves existing citations, annotations and embedded images but cannot add them; math appears as TeX source. See browser limitations for details.

items.title: Accounts and personal settings
items.text: Open Settings to manage your profile, sign-in methods, language, API keys and connected applications.

items.title: Accounts
items.text:
Register from the sign-in page if registration is open, or follow a group invitation link. Otherwise, ask the instance administrator to create an account.

Sign in with a password, a passkey, or an institutional provider when offered. An instance may require institutional sign-in and hide local sign-in options.

If you already have an account, connect an institutional provider under Settings → Sign-in and security before using it to sign in. Matching email addresses do not link accounts automatically.

Forgot your password? Use the reset link on the sign-in page if it is available. Self-service reset needs a confirmed email address. Otherwise, ask the administrator for a reset.

After repeated incorrect passwords or codes, sign-in pauses for up to five minutes. Wait before retrying; reloading or requesting another code does not clear the pause.

items.title: Account settings
items.text:
Use Profile to change your display name, email address and publication visibility. Confirm a new email address using the link altero sends you.

Under Sign-in and security, you can change your password, manage sign-in methods and sign out individual browser sessions. Sensitive changes may ask you to confirm your identity again; that confirmation lasts five minutes. On an instance that requires institutional sign-in, use your provider to confirm.

items.title: Passkeys
items.text:
A passkey lets you sign in using your device's fingerprint, face recognition or PIN, without typing a username or password. It also satisfies identity confirmation for sensitive actions.

Add or remove passkeys under Sign-in and security. Keep another way to sign in if a passkey lives on just one device. The interface will not let you remove your last sign-in method.

If passkeys are unavailable, ask the administrator whether they are enabled for this server address.

items.title: Second factors
items.text:
You can add an authenticator app or email codes to password sign-in:

  • Authenticator app: scan the setup code, then enter a code from the app to finish setup.
  • Email codes: first confirm your email address, then enable this option. Codes expire after ten minutes and work only in the browser that requested them.

If both are enabled, altero asks for the authenticator code first. Choose Use a code by email instead if you cannot access the app. Passkey sign-in does not require an additional code. On an institutional-only instance, manage second factors with your identity provider.

items.title: API keys
items.text:
Open Settings → API keys to create, review or revoke keys used by Zotero Desktop and other tools. Each entry shows its permissions and recent use.

Copy a new key immediately: it is shown in full only once. Treat it like a password. Revoke a key you no longer recognize or need; any client using it will lose access immediately.

Browser sign-in and API keys are separate. To connect Zotero Desktop, use Link Account.

items.title: Connected applications
items.text:
Settings → Connected applications lists applications you have approved, their permissions and recent use. Choose Disconnect to stop an application's access immediately.

When an application asks to connect, sign in to altero, review its requested permissions, and choose which libraries or collections it may reach. Approve only access you intend to give. Operators can find registration instructions in Connecting other applications.

items.title: Language and time zone
items.text:
Choose your language and time zone in Settings. Both preferences follow your account across browsers; by default they follow the browser.

The interface supports regional English, Portuguese and Chinese variants, as well as right-to-left languages. Dates follow your regional format and chosen time zone. Library content keeps its own text direction.

Some item types and field labels may remain in English where Zotero does not provide a translation. To report or improve wording, see the translation guide.

items.title: Moving, importing and exporting data
items.text:
Choose the tool that matches your goal:

Goal Tool Move your personal library from zotero.org Settings → Import and export, migration from zotero.org Back up a library or move it between altero instances An altero library archive Use references in another application Export… in the library view

items.title: Moving in from zotero.org
items.text:
This is a one-time copy, not continuing synchronization between servers.

  1. Finish syncing to zotero.org, back up your library and pause edits.
  2. In zotero.org's account settings, create an API key with read access to your personal library.
  3. Open altero's migration screen under Settings → Import and export and enter that key. Your zotero.org password is not needed.
  4. Review the target library. Migration replaces its contents only if you explicitly allow replacement; it does not merge libraries.
  5. Start the copy, wait for completion, and review the summary for skipped items or missing files.
  6. Follow Connecting a Zotero client before switching the desktop application.

The copy preserves object identifiers and sync versions. The temporary zotero.org key is used for the copy and is not stored. Group libraries are not imported.

Important

A Zotero profile that has synced before remembers its account number. Linking to a different account is refused. Ask the administrator about preserving the original account number, or use a fresh profile; see A profile that has synced before.

Only files present on zotero.org can be copied. Linked files, files not uploaded there, and WebDAV files are absent. Keep a client or backup that holds them. For WebDAV, you can keep the existing file server or upload the local files to altero.

Use a single server process for browser migration and avoid restarting it while the copy runs. Check the result before reconnecting clients. For shell migration, see Administration.

items.title: Import and export
items.text:
An altero archive contains a complete library's objects, sync history and stored attachment bytes. Accounts, API keys and instance configuration are not included. For a complete server backup, follow Backups.

Under Settings → Import and export, choose a library and export its archive. For a group, an administrator may export; only its owner may restore.

To restore, select the target library and an archive. Confirm your identity when asked. A non-empty library is left unchanged unless you explicitly enable replacement.

Warning

Replacement discards the target library's existing contents, including files. Keep a backup and pause client edits first. Restoring an older archive does not automatically rewind already-synchronized desktop copies. Follow the recovery procedure before resuming sync.

items.title: Export references for another application
items.text:
Use Export… above the item list or in the detail or selection pane. Choose which references to include and a format such as BibTeX, RIS, CSV or CSL JSON. An export follows the selected view or search past the end of the loaded page.

Reference exports do not include attachment bytes or a complete sync history and are unsuitable as server backups. See Writing items out.

items.title: Groups, invitations and activity
items.text: Open Groups in the header to see your memberships, create a group or manage a group you administer. Open a group library from the library sidebar to work with its references.

items.title: Groups
items.text:
Any signed-in user can create a group. Its settings control visibility, reading, item editing and file uploads. Group administrators manage these settings and membership; see Group policy.

A member can also have a restriction: read only, edit only their own items, or add and edit without removing. These restrictions cannot grant more access than the group's policy. Some desktop operations may produce sync errors when a member's restriction forbids them.

Public metadata does not make a group's attachment files public. Files remain available to members, subject to their permissions.

Members can leave a group. Only the owner can transfer ownership or delete it. Deleting a group permanently removes its library; there is no group Trash.

items.title: Notifications and invitations
items.text:
A group administrator can invite someone by email and choose their role and permissions. Existing users with that confirmed address see the invitation in notifications. An emailed invitation link also lets someone register before accepting, even when general registration is closed.

Open the invitation and sign in or register with the address it names. Accept or decline it on that screen. Without the invitation link, confirm your email address before accepting. Registration alone does not join the group.

If a link no longer works, ask the group administrator for a new invitation.

items.title: What has happened in a group
items.text:
Every member can read recent activity in the group's panel: who changed items, collections or membership, and when. Entries show titles as they were at the time, including for objects later renamed or deleted.

Activity is a summary, rather than a field-by-field edit history. An item's details also show who added it and who last changed it.

items.title: Hearing about a group
items.text:
In each group's panel, choose whether to receive notifications about:

  • items added or changed;
  • items deleted;
  • people joining or leaving;
  • collections added or changed.

All categories are off by default. Your choices affect only your own notifications for that group.

Notifications appear in the interface. When mail is configured, altero can also send a digest after changes settle. It does not email you a digest about your own changes. See Group notifications for delivery timing.

items.title: Web interface implementation notes
items.text: This reference is for contributors changing the browser interface. For user tasks, see the web guide.

items.title: Building it
items.text:
Built into the container image already. From a source checkout:

cd web
npm ci
npm run build        # writes into src/altero/web/static
npm test
npm run dev          # localhost:5173, proxying the API to :8000

Without that build the server still runs and the API is fully usable; /app/ answers 503 and says what to run.

items.title: End-to-end tests
items.text:
npm run e2e drives the built interface in Chromium, at desktop and phone sizes, against a real server on a throwaway SQLite database. It fails on any Content-Security-Policy violation and on serious or critical axe findings. Build first; the first run needs npx playwright install chromium.

Tests cover editing, merging, files, sharing, account security, translated controls, right-to-left layout, touch and keyboard interaction, motion, and app update behavior. Verify persisted API state as well as rendered feedback. These Chromium checks do not establish Safari, native-device or screen-reader compatibility, and catalog checks do not replace linguistic review.

When reopening a seeded item, use libraryRow or openItem so fixtures beyond the first page are loaded. Scroll drag targets into view. Clean up temporary paging and tree fixtures so a test does not depend on suite order.

items.title: Design
items.text:
Use the shared design system, surface classes and tokens. Theme selection follows the operating system unless the user overrides it. Style guards check surface use, contrast, fonts and logical CSS properties.

Fonts are self-hosted IBM Plex Sans, with Japanese, Arabic and Hebrew faces. Use the supplied stylesheets and font-display: swap; script-specific sheets load on demand. Keep package installation scripts disabled to avoid telemetry. No font request should reach a third party.

Use logical start/end properties for right-to-left layout. Mixed-language content determines its own direction. Verify mouse, touch and splitter-key behavior in both directions.

Tags share TagPill.vue, styles/tag-pills.css and ordering in items/tags.ts. The component owns rename drafts and errors; callers provide library filtering or item-only removal. Pending additions and removals project over current tags without mutating synced item versions. Queued writes rebase; a refused write removes only its own projection. Navigation discards unsent operations.

items.title: Durable sign-in budgets
items.text:
services/loginlimits.py reserves an account and address allowance in login_attempts. Reservations commit before verification so concurrent requests and worker restarts share a budget; no database lock spans password hashing. Call before changing other state in the session. Password sign-in and both TOTP/email completion paths use these reservations; the API layer supplies the trusted connection address and maps a refusal to JSON 429 with a whole-second Retry-After.

Account and address rows are locked in sorted key order on both SQLite and PostgreSQL. A successful proof clears only its account reservation's generation and refunds exactly one address attempt. An older success cannot erase a newer account guess or refund a new address window after expiry. Identifiers are SHA-256 hashes with separate namespaces; these are pseudonymous counters, not encrypted personal data. Idle rows expire after fifteen minutes and are pruned by the next reservation.

Username and email aliases resolve to the same user id before reserving the password budget. Unknown identifiers use the same limits with normalized names. TOTP and email share a second-factor budget by user id, so a new pending session, a resend or a factor switch cannot reset it. The existing five-guess limit on each emailed code remains in force independently.

items.title: The note editor
items.text:
The editor uses Tiptap with a port of Zotero's note schema, HTML parsing, serialization and keymap in web/src/notes/. Differential checks and the recorded corpus protect round trips with the desktop editor. Load it on demand. Disable Tiptap's injected stylesheet for CSP compatibility; use notes/editor.css.

Toolbar menus use fixed viewport positions. Apply those coordinates before moving keyboard focus into the menu: focusing the unpositioned list can scroll the document, whose scroll handler then dismisses it. Focus also disables native ancestor scrolling; only the menu list scrolls to reveal the selected option. Scroll notifications dismiss the menu when its anchor moves. A notification queued while the trigger was focused can arrive after opening and must leave the menu open when its anchor is unchanged. The browser regression opens New Note below a populated collection sidebar and checks that the menu stays open without moving the page.

items.title: Undoing filing and trash changes
items.text:
PATCH /web/libraries/{id}/items returns an undo object alongside items. Its version is the committed library watermark; its items hold each changed item's prior collections and/or deleted value. Unchanged properties and items are omitted. The snapshot comes from stored state under the write lock, so it includes memberships the browser had not loaded.

POST /web/libraries/{id}/items/undo accepts that items array with If-Unmodified-Since-Version set to the returned version. It requires the browser session, CSRF token and current item permissions. The version must match exactly under the write lock: a later sync, edit or undo returns 412 without changing anything. Every item is restored in one transaction and one new library version. Only collection memberships and trash state can be restored here; permanent deletion and merge graphs are outside this endpoint. The browser does not persist these snapshots across page reloads.

Filing, trashing and restoring through the library store show the offer after the write commits. A failed list refresh does not report the write as failed or invite a second write. Undo remains bound to its original library after navigation; an open parent's children are refreshed as well. A refusal is reported in the toast region, with a separate message for a stale watermark.

POST /web/libraries/{source}/items/copy returns the same undo shape, with the destination library version and newly created root keys set to deleted: true. Send it to the destination's undo endpoint. This moves the copies and their child graphs into its Trash without deleting their bytes or changing the originals. A source-library edit does not invalidate this offer; a destination edit does. The response contains undo: null when the caller may copy but cannot remove records there, such as an add-only group member. Permissions are checked again when undo runs.

items.title: Duplicate merge endpoint
items.text:
The duplicates listing accepts grouped=true with scope=duplicates. It returns groups (lists of item keys), totalGroups, and the usual item envelopes and library watermark. In this mode start and limit count groups. Search, tag and collection filters find groups; every member readable by the viewer is included, oldest first. The requested sort orders groups by their first matching record. Without grouped, the existing item-based pagination is unchanged.

The export endpoint accepts the same grouped=true flag, expanding matching groups before writing them in batches. Explicit group-member selections export by key with scope=all, so the current search cannot remove a selected member.

The library store requests group pages and selects a whole group from any member. Select-all stays within the active group. Explicit individual inspection remains available, and an append at a different watermark restarts group pagination.

Groups are connected components of the existing candidate matches. A matching identifier can connect records whose titles differ, and a title match can connect another record to that group. Membership is a suggestion for review, not a claim that every pair has the same identifier or item type.

The comparison follows the desktop's master-and-field-choice model, reviewed in duplicatesMergePane.js and itemBox.js. The browser uses native select controls instead of desktop field popups. Group selection, individual inspection and membership changes have ordinary click/tap controls; coarse pointers retain 44-pixel targets. On a narrow screen, activating a group reveals its pane and closing it returns focus to the group.

The duplicates pane uses POST /web/libraries/{id}/items/merge, authenticated by the browser session and CSRF token. It accepts:

{
  "master": "MASTER22",
  "others": ["DUPL2345"],
  "fields": {
    "title": "Chosen title",
    "creators": [{"creatorType": "author", "name": "A collective"}]
  }
}

Send If-Unmodified-Since-Version with the library version at which the items were read. The version must match exactly, checked under the library lock. An absent header answers 428; a stale or future one answers 412. On 412, read the selected items again and review the choices before retrying.

The browser prepares a separate review snapshot with scope=all and the selected keys, in batches of at most 100. Every batch must report the same library version and include every selected key. Live list refreshes do not advance that snapshot's version. Confirmation sends it once; a failed list refresh after a committed merge does not turn success into an invitation to submit the merge again.

The items must be untrashed regular items of one type in this library, named once each. fields is optional: omitted fields and creators stay on the master, text or null replaces a bibliographic field, and a creators array replaces the whole creator list. An empty string or null clears a field; creators: [] clears creators. Structural properties, type changes and timestamps are refused. Tags, collections and relations are combined by the merge itself, including attachment deduplication and child moves, in one new library version.

The 200 response includes items, with the master first and each changed item in its ordinary envelope. Last-Modified-Version gives their shared new version. An optional locale query selects the interface language for PDF word ordering; it defaults to the account language, then en-US.

It also returns undo: {"version": N, "merge": true}. To reverse that merge, send POST /web/libraries/{id}/items/merge/undo with the session, CSRF token and If-Unmodified-Since-Version: N. The request carries no item data. A private database snapshot holds the prior values of precisely the properties changed by the merge, including incoming relations and attachment/annotation parents. Only the person who merged can use it; all current item permissions apply again.

The library and stored merge versions must both match under the write lock. A later write or retry answers 412, even if the caller supplies a newer version. A missing, expired or another person's snapshot answers 404. Each library keeps at most one snapshot, for five minutes; a subsequent merge replaces it. The retention sweep removes expired snapshots, and clearing/restoring a library removes its snapshot. Snapshots are excluded from library archives.

Undo restores the old fields, creators, tags, collections, dates added, trash states, note HTML and relations at one new library version. It never rewinds sync versions or changes registered file bytes/full text. Notes promoted from attachment text during the merge go to Trash; their original text returns to the attachment. A refused reversal rolls back every change and keeps the snapshot available until it expires or the library changes.

An inverse that effectively changes only relations keeps the current dateModified, as ordinary browser relationship edits do. On undeleting a duplicate, Zotero removes its survivor's merge-tracking relation itself while preserving that date, and can skip the now-redundant remote update. Other restored content receives the normal new modification timestamp.

items.title: Not built yet
items.text:
Items, notes and attachments can be created and edited in the browser, and duplicate items can be merged. Remaining browser gaps include:

  • An integrated PDF reader and annotation tools.
  • Offline library access. The installed app opens offline, but library data is not stored on the device.
  • Advanced search and a saved-search builder.
  • Adding items by DOI, ISBN or PMID.
  • A citation-style picker and a multi-item bibliography or report interface. The server already renders bibliographies and reports; the detail pane's citation uses format=bib.
  • Deleting a tag from the whole library at once.

Moving in from zotero.org brings the personal library only; a group has to be made here and its members invited.

For account and server operations, see Administration.

items.title: Browsing and organizing a library
items.text: Choose My Library or a group in the sidebar. Select a collection or view on the left, an item in the middle, and use its details on the right. Browser changes synchronize with Zotero Desktop.

items.title: Browsing a library
items.text:
Select the library name to show its top-level items. Expand collections with their arrows. Recently Read, Duplicate Items, Unfiled Items and Trash offer other ways to find records. My Publications appears only in your personal library.

Use search to find references and tags to narrow the list. Selecting several tags requires all of them. Use Show more to load more items. Drag the dividers to resize the panes; your browser remembers their widths.

Open a child note or attachment from its parent. Close details returns to that parent. Attachments can be opened or downloaded. The citation section renders a reference in the style you choose.

items.title: Editing an item
items.text:
• Create: press + above the list and choose an item type. The new item goes into the current collection.
  • Edit fields: select a value, type, then press Enter or leave the field to save. Escape cancels. Use Shift+Enter to save multi-line fields such as Abstract and Extra.
  • Change type: use the type menu. Review the warning if the new type cannot hold some fields.
  • Edit creators: choose a role and enter names. More Options… switches to a single name for an organization and offers reordering; the grip can also be dragged.
  • Edit tags: use + under Tags, the pencil to rename one on this item, or × to remove it from this item.
  • Relate items: use + under Related, search, and select a result. − removes the relationship from both items.
  • Set rights: use the license chooser beside Rights, or enter other rights text.

An item in Trash must be restored before editing. In a read-only library, editing controls are unavailable.

Changes made elsewhere appear while the page is open. If someone changes the same field while you are editing, review the local and remote values and choose which to keep. Tags are applied on top of current tags.

items.title: Writing a note
items.text:
Use the note button above the list to create a New Standalone Note or a New Item Note. + beside an item's Notes adds a child note.

Select text for formatting tools. On a phone or tablet, the tools sit above the keyboard. Type / at the start of a line or after a space to choose a block type. Common shortcuts and Markdown-style headings and lists also work. The full-screen button gives you more room to write.

Notes save after you stop typing; Saved. confirms completion. If the note changed elsewhere, choose between the local and remote versions.

Existing Zotero citations, annotations and embedded images are preserved but cannot be added here. Math appears as TeX source. Notes in an unsupported newer format open read-only.

items.title: Adding files and links
items.text:
Task Action Attach a file to an item Attach File…, + beside Attachments, or drop a file onto the item Add a standalone file Add File…, or drop a file onto the library, collection or item list Attach a web address Attach Web Link… and enter the URL Rename a file Edit Filename in the attachment details Replace its contents Replace File… in the attachment details

Uploads show progress and a cancel button. Add individual files; folders cannot be dropped. The default file limit is 1 GiB, but your administrator may set a different limit. Group policy may prevent file uploads.

Renaming a file keeps its title. Replacing it keeps the attachment record and title but uses the new file's name. If another person replaced the file while yours was uploading, reload before trying again.

items.title: Collections
items.text:
Use + on a library row to create a top-level collection, or on a collection to create a subcollection. Open a collection's settings to rename, move or delete it. You can also drag it onto another collection or the library row.

Deleting a collection leaves its items in the library and promotes its subcollections. It does not delete the references or files.

To give others a read-only link, open Share a link… in the collection settings. See Sharing one collection.

items.title: Items
items.text: Use Move or copy…, Move to trash, Restore or Delete in the detail pane. For several items, select them first; the pane then offers actions for the selection.

items.title: Selecting items
items.text:
• Ctrl-click, or Cmd-click on a Mac, adds or removes a row.
  • Shift-click selects a range.
  • Ctrl/Cmd-A selects the loaded page, or the active duplicate group.
  • Select shows checkboxes for touch and keyboard use.

Arrow keys move through the list. Enter opens the details; F2 edits the title. Press ? for the full shortcut list.

items.title: Moving and copying
items.text:
Drop target Result A collection in the same library Add membership; keep existing memberships A collection while holding Shift Move from the current collection to the target The current library row Remove from the current collection Another library Copy the item, notes, attachments and tags; keep the original Trash Move the item to Trash

A drag starting on a selected row carries the selection. Starting on another row carries only that item. Move or copy… provides the same operations without dragging, including the option to remove items from the current collection.

items.title: Trash and undo
items.text:
Delete on the keyboard moves an item to Trash. In Trash, it asks to delete permanently. Empty Trash removes all trashed items after confirmation. Permanent deletion cannot be undone.

To trash a child note or attachment, open its details from the parent. To recover it later, select it in Trash and choose Restore. Restoring a child does not restore its parent.

After filing, trashing, restoring, copying or merging, Undo appears briefly in the confirmation message. A later change to the library can make undo unavailable. If the message is gone, trashed items can still be restored from Trash. Undoing a copy moves the new copies to the destination's Trash.

items.title: Merging duplicates
items.text:
1. Open Duplicate Items and select a group. Check that the records describe the same work.
  2. Choose the master record; the oldest is selected by default.
  3. Choose the field values and creator list to keep. Use Select to exclude a record that does not belong.
  4. Press Merge Items, review the warning and confirm.

Merging needs at least two items of the same type and permission to edit and remove them. It combines collections, tags, related items and children, then moves the other records to Trash. Matching attachments may be combined; files with notes are kept separately where needed for safe Zotero synchronization.

Use Undo in the confirmation message to reverse a merge while it is still available. Restoring an individual duplicate from Trash later does not reverse the merged fields or move children back. If the library changed during review, reload and check the records again.

items.title: Writing items out
items.text:
Choose Export… above the list or in the detail or selection pane. Select the current selection, filtered view or whole library, then an export format. Export includes all matching references, beyond the loaded page.

Formats include BibTeX, BibLaTeX, CSL JSON, RIS, CSV and the other supported Zotero export formats. These files contain references, without attachment bytes or standalone notes and annotations. For complete backups, use a library archive.

items.title: By touch
items.text: Tap Select to work with several items using checkboxes. Hold a row briefly before dragging; moving immediately scrolls instead. Accepted destinations are highlighted. Use Move or copy… for operations that otherwise require keyboard modifiers.

items.title: Tags
items.text:
Selecting a sidebar tag filters the list. Its pencil renames it throughout the library, including items outside the current view. Renaming onto an existing name combines the tags. This has no undo.

For a change to just one item, edit tags in that item's details instead.

items.title: Publishing and sharing
items.text: Use My Publications for work you want listed on your profile. Use a shared-collection link for a reading list or other collection that anyone holding the link can open.

items.title: My Publications
items.text:
Publish one work at a time from its details or by dragging it onto My Publications in your personal library.

The publishing dialog asks you to:

  1. Choose whether to include files and notes.
  2. Confirm that the work is yours and that you may distribute any included files.
  3. Choose rights for shared files, or keep the existing Rights field.

Linked files cannot be published because their bytes are not on the server. Group libraries do not have My Publications.

Change a license later using the item's Rights field. In My Publications, you can show or hide individual child notes and attachments.

To stop listing a work, use the remove button in its details or press Delete in My Publications. The work and files remain in your library. Removing a listing does not withdraw a license you have already granted.

items.title: Profile pages
items.text: Your profile is at /app/u/<username>. It lists published work, with abstracts, rights, citations and any notes or files you chose to publish.

items.title: Who can see it
items.text:
Choose the audience under Settings → Profile:

Audience Who can open the published work Anyone Anyone, without an account; the default People with an account here People signed into this altero instance Nobody The profile is hidden; your library and publication choices remain

These settings also govern public API access to the publications. Your own Zotero client can still synchronize them.

items.title: Sharing one collection
items.text:
Open the collection's settings and choose Share a link…. Creating a link requires write access to the library.

Choose:

  • the collection alone or its subcollections too;
  • whether readers can open attachment files;
  • an expiry date, or no expiry.

Create the link and copy it immediately. It is shown only once. If copying fails, select the displayed URL and copy it manually. Replace a lost link with a new one.

Anyone holding a working link can read the shared collection without an account. The view follows changes to that collection, but does not provide sync access or reveal the rest of the library or its Trash.

Review existing links in the same dialog and revoke those you no longer need. Expired, revoked or deleted links stop working. Deleting the collection also removes its links.
